title: Wendell and the Lantern
premise: In the river city of Vellamark, 1848, Yara Montrose cuts type by lantern light in her father's print shop while revolution gathers in the streets. When a sealed letter arrives naming her family as conspirators in a plot they never joined, the authorities give them one night before the ice breaks on the river and the last ferry departs. Yara discovers her father has been printing seditious pamphlets to protect his brother, a true revolutionary, and that the letter was sent by someone inside their own household. In the end, Yara gives the final berth to her father's brother, keeps her father beside her to face the inquiry, and learns that belonging is not a place you flee to but a choice you make in the open.
about_author: Jude Montrose is the pen name of a former typesetter who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century letterpress equipment before turning to fiction. Their work draws on family archives of émigré printers who fled the revolutions of 1848.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the print shop on the eve of unrest, Yara sorts type by candlelight while soldiers patrol outside and her father burns papers he claims are old invoices. Her younger brother Tomas counts what can be carried into one satchel each. The emotional beat is quiet dread: a family practicing invisibility so well they've nearly convinced themselves it's safety.

chapters.title: A Letter Under Seal
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A government courier delivers a sealed letter naming the Montroses in a conspiracy plot, with one berth reserved on the last ferry before the ice breaks. Searching for answers, Yara finds seditious pamphlets hidden in the type cases—printed in her father's hand—and realizes her uncle Wendell, the 'lantern' of her childhood stories, is the true target. Rising tension: the family's invisibility was always a borrowed lie.

chapters.title: What the Ice Will Take
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, climax. On the final night, Yara confronts her father and discovers the informant is Tomas, who traded the letter for his own passage. At the frozen dock, with soldiers closing in, she must decide who takes the single berth. She puts Wendell aboard, chooses to stand with her father, and publicly names herself as the printer's daughter—the opposite of invisible.

chapters.title: The Last Impression
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, resolution. Weeks later, under house inquiry, Yara and her father reopen the shop, printing an honest account of the plot to clear Wendell's name from afar. Tomas returns, unasked, and is given work rather than forgiveness too easily. The emotional beat is earned belonging: Yara hangs the lantern in the window, no longer hiding, measuring the world now in what can be said aloud.
